comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological rigor (C28-C33). Both evaluations rate the LC-MS methodology, sample size, and statistical validation as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes repeatability values and p-values, while peer reviewers praise the unified methodology and specificity advantages over previous assays.

Perfect agreement on descriptive statistics (C34-C45). Both evaluations rate these order-level glucose measurements as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with body mass effects, while peer reviewers emphasize the novel contribution of this unified dataset to avian glycemia research.

Divergent evaluations on lysine number findings (C50-C51). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to limited variation and small sample size, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating it as part of thorough analysis without raising concerns about the negative finding.

Divergent evaluations on study limitations (C71-C73). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, viewing the authors' acknowledgment of limitations as appropriate transparency. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting handling time concerns but concluding limitations make findings more conservative rather than invalid.

Strong agreement on body mass-glucose relationship (C5, C39, C74). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED with significant statistical evidence. OpenEval emphasizes phylogenetic controls and Figure 2A visualization (C79), while peer reviewers accept it as established within POLS framework.

Strong agreement on glycation resistance findings (C3, C4, C46, C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED with convincing evidence. OpenEval emphasizes the non-linear relationship with slope <1 and mathematical soundness, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the glucose-glycation correlation as a key result. OpenEval also includes visual support claims (C82, C83) not mentioned by peer reviewers.

Strong agreement on longevity-glucose relationship (C6, C66, C75). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the significant quadratic term and Figure 2B (C80), while peer reviewers note this finding as 'somewhat surprising' but treat it as valid and convincing evidence.

Strong agreement on paradoxical glycation-longevity finding (C8, C9, C53, C76). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the paradox of glycation differences without glucose differences, while peer reviewers note it as surprising but accept it without methodological concerns. OpenEval includes C81 (Figure 3) not in peer evaluation; peer reviewers include diet findings (C52, C67).

Agreement on POLS contradiction (C68). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval (C7, C68) emphasizes the distinction between body mass effects (aligning with POLS) and other traits (contradicting POLS), while peer reviewers frame it within POLS framework and accept findings that contrast with previous studies.

Partial overlap on diet effects (C52, C67). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting non-significant diet effects in Table 1 as a clear negative finding. Peer reviewers include these claims in their broader evaluation of surprising findings (R4) alongside glycation-longevity results, rating the combined set as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluated mechanistic explanations (C10, C54-C60) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are explicitly speculative with no direct measurements in the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval evaluated the flamingo observation (C69) as SUPPORTED, treating it as a straightforward secondary finding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific observational claim.

OpenEval evaluated the Procellariiformes interpretation (C70) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is explicitly speculative and requires additional physiological data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this mechanistic distinction.

OpenEval evaluated background claims establishing the central paradox (C1, C2, C16, C20, C61) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these motivating background claims.

OpenEval evaluated main conclusion summary claims (C62-C65) as SUPPORTED, noting they accurately reflect study findings. Peer reviewers reference C64 in R1 but do not provide a separate evaluation of the summary conclusions as a group.

OpenEval evaluated literature background and hypotheses (C11-C27) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and distinction between established facts and hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these background literature claims.

OpenEval evaluated prior comparative work citations (C40, C47-C49) as SUPPORTED, contextualizing current findings with established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these literature contextualization claims.
